thread:
maria: Proposal: implement tenant-aware exporter fanout + per-tenant retention TTL in the telemetry pipeline. idea is to tag spans with tenant_id at service edge, let collector route to per-tenant buckets/backends, enforce retention and backpressure there. thoughts?

raj: +1 on routing in collector, avoids SDK complexity. main worry is memory blowup if a noisy tenant sends spikes. how do we backpressure? :thinking_face:

ellen: We Need bounded queues per-tenant, not unbounded. collector can maintain a fixed buffer per-tenant and evict/drop with policy when full (drop-oldest or reject-new). dropping has tradeoffs for evals.

maria: Agreed. My mental model: SDK adds resource.attribute tenant_id, collector uses routing/receivers to fanout into tenant-specific exporters or to a multitenant backend with a retention tag. Collector config sketch:
```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, attributes]
      exporters: [tenant_router]
exporters:
  tenant_router:
    plugin: multiroute # pseudo-config - route by resource.tenant_id -> backend/retention
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: resource.tenant.id
        action: insert
```

zhou: Collector-side routing is great. but we need to decide: do we physically fanout to separate storage/exporter instances per-tenant, or add tenant metadata and let a single exporter enforce retention? fanout = isolation but more resource usage. single exporter + tags = simpler.

sam: For noisy tenants, physical fanout lets us hot-shed one tenant without impacting others. but costlier. Maybe hybrid: small % of tenants get dedicated exporters (SLA/customers) and rest go to multitenant path.

ellen: Important: SDK behavior matters. Python/Go/Rust differences here. Python's BatchSpanProcessor has an internal queue_size and max_queue_size env var (OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE) and worker thread. Go SDK uses a channel with buffer and goroutine; Rust also has a bounded worker queue. We need consistent defaults and environment variables across our infra packages to avoid surprises.

maria: We're also debating telemetry-agent vs direct SDK export. If we route from services directly to collector (hosted) vs sidecar, TLS and MTLS complexity rises. I prefer sidecar for private deploys and direct collector for hosted.

raj: Backpressure options: (1) block application (bad), (2) drop spans (acceptable for sampling), (3) return error to app (otlp client returns error) which will cause application retries (worse). So bounded queue + drop-oldest/new with a metric emitted when drop occurs. Have collector emit dropped_span_count metric per-tenant.

maria: Good point. Need a standard metric label: telemetry.dropped_spans.reason and telemetry.dropped_spans.tenant_id. console should have per-tenant drop rates.

ellen: About retention TTL: collector can add a header or metadata to exporter that instructs storage to expire after N days. For backends that don't support TTL, we can run an expirer job. For dedicated customers, allow override via account config service with an API that collector polls.

sam: Implementation detail: don't let routing logic in collector do heavy lookups per-span (DB call). Keep account configs cached in memory with TTL + watch via etcd/k8s configmap. config changes should be eventual consistent.

zhou: Language SDKs - we should ship small opinionated init shims per language that set: OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, resource attr mapping (tenant_id from request headers), BatchSpanProcessor params (max_queue_size, scheduled_delay_millis, max_export_batch_size) and graceful shutdown hook. Example envs: REDWOOD_OTEL_QUEUE=2000, REDWOOD_OTEL_BATCH_MS=200.

maria: Example python snippet for middleware to attach tenant_id:
```python
from opentelemetry import trace
tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)

def attach_tenant(span, tenant_id):
    span.set_attribute("tenant.id", tenant_id)

with tracer.start_as_current_span("handle_req") as span:
    attach_tenant(span, req.headers.get("x-tenant-id"))
    ...
```

raj: Also ensure stable resource attributes (resource detection) to avoid high cardinality on traces. tenant_id is high-card but required; still avoid adding request ids or user ids in resource attrs. Put those as span attributes only when necessary.

ellen: Shutdown semantics: all three SDKs require explicit provider.shutdown() or equivalent in lifecycle hooks. We should ensure our platform agents call shutdown on SIGTERM and wait up to N seconds (configurable) before force exit. For Python, asyncio apps need to await tracer_provider.shutdown(). For Go, tracerprovider.Shutdown(ctx). For Rust, opentelemetry::global::shutdown_tracer_provider();

sam: Re: retries and ordering: if collector does per-tenant buffering, exporter retries can reorder spans. If ordering is critical (rare), recommend client-side buffering + seq numbers, but that's heavy. We'll document ordering caveats.

maria: UX: console should expose per-tenant retention, current buffer utilization, drop rate, and sampling rate. Also a toggle to promote tenant to dedicated exporter.

zhou: Security: tenant_id propagation must be authenticated. do not accept x-tenant-id from arbitrary headers in hosted mode unless mTLS or token verifies tenant. Otherwise spoofing risk.

ellen: Quick poll: prefer collector routing + bounded per-tenant buffer + metric exports for drops + sidecar for private. thumbs?

maria: @channel please react. I think we have consensus on approach, next steps: 1) implement collector routing prototype (zhou + raj), 2) add SDK init shims and env vars (ellen + sam), 3) dashboard wires (maria). I'll open RFC today.

telemetry-bot: Created RFC ticket INF-4321: "Tenant-aware telemetry routing & retention" assigned to zhou, raj, ellen, sam, due in 2 weeks.

raj: I'll start with a small collector pipeline and a tenant-buffered processor PoC. will ping when PR up.

ellen: I'll draft the SDK init shims and a short migration guide for services. include graceful shutdown snippet.

sam: I'll prototype dashboard panels for drop rates and buffer saturation.

maria: Awesome. Thanks all. :heart:
